description: The Energy Policy Simulator is a free, open-source system dynamics model that estimates how climate and energy policies change emissions, costs, jobs and health. It is developed by Energy Innovation LLC in its Energy Policy Solutions project, with Jeff Rissman, Robbie Orvis and Todd Fincannon among the creators, to show policymakers which policies cut greenhouse gases most effectively with the best financial and health outcomes. Users set many policy levers, such as a carbon tax, vehicle fuel economy standards, methane leak reduction or faster technology research, across transport, electricity supply, buildings, industry, agriculture and land use, plus hydrogen supply and district heat. Annual outputs include emissions of 12 pollutants, cash-flow effects on government, industries, labour, consumers and energy suppliers, jobs, GDP and wages in 42 categories, avoided deaths and other health outcomes, electricity capacity and generation by source, and vehicle fleet shares. Coverage is the United States in the eps-us release, with a modular design that lets other regions swap input data. It is accessible in a web browser or downloadable to run with the free Vensim Model Reader, with source on GitHub under GPL 3.0 at no cost. Caveats: it is a policy screening model, not a grid or dispatch model. Simulation uses are long-term decarbonisation scenarios for the electricity and fuel sectors. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
